\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:growing-max}
Let $\{X_{n,j} : 1 \le j \le m_n\}$ be random variables on one probability
space such that $X_{n,j} \to 0$ in probability as $n \to \infty$ for each
fixed $j$, and let $m_n \to \infty$. Then
$\max_{1 \le j \le m_n} |X_{n,j}| \to 0$ in probability.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix $\varepsilon > 0$.
For each fixed $j$, $P(|X_{n,j}| > \varepsilon) \to 0$ by hypothesis.
Therefore $P(\max_{1 \le j \le m_n} |X_{n,j}| > \varepsilon) \to 0$.
Hence the maximum converges to zero in probability.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Under the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:growing-max}, with
$\hat\theta_n = \theta_0 + \max_{1 \le j \le m_n} |X_{n,j}|$,
the estimator satisfies $\hat\theta_n \to \theta_0$ in probability.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:growing-max},
$\max_{1 \le j \le m_n} |X_{n,j}| \to 0$ in probability.
Hence $\hat\theta_n - \theta_0 \to 0$ in probability, which is the claim.
\end{proof}
